# SpotCheck

> A free toolkit of eight browser bookmarklets for spot-checking web accessibility. Each tool runs entirely client-side against the current page's DOM, requires no installation or extension permissions, and sends nothing to a server. Every tool maps to specific WCAG 2.2 success criteria.

SpotCheck is built and maintained by Homer Gaines, a UI engineer and certified accessibility professional. The tools are dependency-free vanilla JavaScript, and the readable unminified source for each one is published on its page.

Intended use: fast spot-checks during development, code review, and triage. SpotCheck is not a substitute for a full manual audit or for testing with assistive technology. Automated checks catch a minority of accessibility issues, and every tool page states what its check cannot detect.

## Tools

- [Text Contrast Checker](https://www.spotcheck.tools/text-contrast-checker): Measures the contrast ratio of every text block against its effective background color and flags anything below the WCAG AA threshold. Relates to 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) and 1.4.6 Contrast (Enhanced).
- [Landmark Visualizer](https://www.spotcheck.tools/landmark-visualizer): Outlines every ARIA and HTML landmark region on the page and flags regions that are duplicated or missing an accessible name. Relates to 1.3.1 Info and Relationships and 2.4.1 Bypass Blocks.
- [Link Accessibility Auditor](https://www.spotcheck.tools/link-accessibility-auditor): Checks every link for an accessible name and flags generic text such as "click here" or "read more" that gives no context out of order. Relates to 2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context) and 2.4.9 Link Purpose (Link Only).
- [Heading Hierarchy Validator](https://www.spotcheck.tools/heading-validator): Reads the heading outline in document order and flags any level that skips ahead, which breaks screen reader navigation by heading. Relates to 1.3.1 Info and Relationships and 2.4.6 Headings and Labels.
- [Image Alt Text Checker](https://www.spotcheck.tools/alt-text-checker): Outlines every image and reports its alt text, a missing alt attribute, or decorative status. Relates to 1.1.1 Non-text Content.
- [Input Label Checker](https://www.spotcheck.tools/input-label-checker): Shows how each form control gets its accessible name, whether from a label element, aria-label, aria-labelledby, or nothing at all. Relates to 1.3.1 Info and Relationships, 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions, and 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value.
- [Tab Order Visualizer](https://www.spotcheck.tools/tab-order-visualizer): Numbers every focusable element in the order a keyboard will reach it and flags positive tabindex values that desynchronize focus order from visual order. Relates to 2.4.3 Focus Order and 2.4.7 Focus Visible.
- [List Identifier](https://www.spotcheck.tools/list-identifier): Finds empty lists, invalid child elements, and list items outside a list container, all of which corrupt the item count a screen reader announces. Relates to 1.3.1 Info and Relationships.

## How to use a bookmarklet

- [SpotCheck home](https://www.spotcheck.tools/): Drag any tool's button to your browser bookmarks bar, navigate to the page you want to test, then click the bookmark. Results are drawn as outlines on the page with a summary panel. Click the bookmark again to clear. Each tool page includes an inline demo you can run without installing anything, and the full source for review.

## Optional

- [WCAG 2.2 Understanding docs](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/): The W3C explanations for every success criterion referenced above. Each SpotCheck tool page links to the specific criteria it covers.
